# Spatial discretization {#sec-ch04}

This chapter is the semi-discrete operator of one Runge-Kutta stage: everything that turns a cell-averaged
state into a tendency, and nothing that advances it in time. A stage reconstructs the primitive variables to
the faces, solves a Riemann problem on each face to get a single flux there, makes that flux single-valued
across a process seam, takes its divergence, and adds the part of the curvature that is not a flux difference.
Time integration is chapter 7, the well-balanced treatment of the vertical is chapter 5, and the positivity
limiter that runs between the Riemann solve and the divergence is chapter 8.

The chapter has two halves because the second has a derivation thread the first does not. Section 4A is the
operator and its interchangeable parts: the divergence, the reconstruction framework with its six interpolants,
the Riemann framework with its five solvers, seam averaging and the geometric sources. Almost none of that is
written down anywhere in the repository, so it is re-derived here from the code. Section 4B is one idea applied
twice: a finite-volume flux is an average over a face, a solver computes a flux from averages over cells, and
the difference between those is second order in the direction that carries the stratification. That half has a
committed derivation behind it and its own test family.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch04-deps
#| fig-cap: "The dependency map of this chapter. A solid black arrow reads requires, a dashed green arrow reads implies. The reconstruction framework implies a pair of interpolants, and selecting either WENO type implies the matching linear polynomial for the velocity and pressure rows. The geometric sources require a solver that returns a face pressure, which only three of the five provide. Both O(dx1^2) corrections require something of the rest of the chapter: the horizontal one needs the face pressure and the curved-grid moments, and the x1 one acts on the reconstructed velocity. Every edge is stated and cited in the section it comes from."
#| fig-alt: "Ten labelled boxes joined by arrows, with solid arrows for requires and dashed green arrows for implies, and a legend below."
```

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Finite-volume update (@sec-ch04-divergence) | `disable-flux-x1\|x2\|x3` | all on | exact in flux form | `test_cubed_sphere_cell_volume_python` |
| Reconstruction framework (@sec-ch04-framework) | `reconstruct/{type,scale,shock}` | `dc`, false, false | set by the interpolant | `test_plm` |
| Donor cell (@sec-ch04-dc) | `type: dc` | the default | 1 | `test_plm` |
| PLM (@sec-ch04-plm) | `type: plm` | off | 2, 1 at an extremum | `test_plm` |
| Centred cp3, cp5 (@sec-ch04-cp) | `type: cp3`, `cp5` | off | 3, 5 | this chapter's check |
| WENO3, WENO5 (@sec-ch04-weno) | `type: weno3`, `weno5` | off | 3, 5; weno3 is 2 at a critical point | `test_weno` |
| PPM (@sec-ch04-ppm) | `type: ppm` | off | 1: the interpolant is a stub | none |
| Riemann framework (@sec-ch04-riemann) | `riemann-solver/{type,dir}` | `roe`, `omni` | — | `test_riemann` |
| LMARS (@sec-ch04-lmars) | `type: lmars` | off; the decks select it | consistent, 1 in the upwind branch | `test_riemann` |
| HLLC (@sec-ch04-hllc) | `type: hllc` | off | three-wave | `test_riemann` |
| Roe (@sec-ch04-roe) | `type: roe` | the default | linearised, no entropy fix | `test_riemann` |
| Shallow and plume Roe (@sec-ch04-shallow) | `type: shallow-roe`, `plume-roe` | off | plume-roe is Lax-Friedrichs | `test_shallow_splash` |
| Seam averaging (@sec-ch04-seam) | none; split $x_1$ axis | automatic | restores telescoping | `test_x1_seam_split_mp` |
| Spherical-polar sources (@sec-ch04-sphsrc) | none; coordinate type | automatic | exact areas and volume | `test_radial_face_moments` |
| Gnomonic sources (@sec-ch04-gnomonic) | none; coordinate type | automatic | exact solid angle and volume | `test_hydrostatic` |
| Horizontal flux covariance (@sec-ch04-fluxcov) | `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` | off | removes two $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ terms | `test_flux_covariance_rows` |
| $x_1$ mass covariance (@sec-ch04-x1masscov) | `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` | off | 2 becomes 4 in the stored velocity | this chapter's check |

: The schemes of this chapter. "Order" is the spatial order of the discrete operator where that is meaningful;
the Riemann solvers are characterised by their wave structure instead. {#tbl-ch04-schemes}

Three of the entries above record code that does not do what its name says, and they are flagged where they
appear rather than collected here: the PPM interpolant is a stub that returns the cell value, the `plume-roe`
solver is a Lax-Friedrichs flux, and four limiter functions beside the PLM slope are never called.
